newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed while New York rallies.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed while New York rallies.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, recovering from earlier weakness, while New York rallied on news that U.S. interest rates were not moving higher.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 12.76 points to close at 6260.14. But declining issues edged out advances 482 to 475 in the broader market.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed one percent higher at 7303 points after being down one percent earlier in the session.
"It was a significant snap-back in the market today," said RBC Dominion Securities Investment Advisor Ira Katzin.

Wall Street's rally was sparked by the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's decision on Tuesday to keep short-term interest rates steady. The decision was expected by investors and their enthusiasm is expected to continue on Wednesday.
"I think we'll have a continuation of this," Katzin said.
Turnover in Canada's largest equities market was moderate at 83.3 million shares worth C$1.52 billion ($1.11 billion).
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices moved ahead, led by conglomerates, transportation, consumer products and media. Five sectors lost ground, including real estate and golds.
Canadian banks were among the most-active Toronto issues on Tuesday. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, the nation's second largest bank, rose 0.25 to 33.50 on 1.8 million shares.
Royal Bank of Canada added 0.15 to 59.40.
Ashton Mining of Canada Inc. dropped 1.05 to 4.95 after announcing more assay results from its northern Alberta diamond project.
Shares in Canadian Tire Corp Ltd., Canada's largest hard goods retailer, jumped 1.50 to 27.
Food producer Oshawa Group Ltd Class A sank 1.50 to 20.50 after it announced weaker first quarter earnings last week.
